newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates rise even further.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates rise even further.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose further on Wednesday as liquidity was still unevenly divided between participants, dealers saying at least one big bank was still short of liquidity.

Dealers said call money, rising to an occasional bid price of 3.375 percent, might go down to the usual level of around 3.06 percent on Friday when the Dutch central banks allocates new liquidity under a fresh special advances pact.
The Dutch central bank will set a new advances pact this afternoon at 1400 GMT. Market players expected an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent for the pact.
"The central bank might allocate more liquidity on Friday under the new pact to solve the shortage of cash for some participants," said one.
Call money was bid between 3.25 and 3.375 percent on Wednesday versus 3.18 on Tuesday.
Other rates were unchanged, with three-month deposits bid at 3.12 percent and one-year paper at 3.34 percent.
"It is a strange situation that some bids for call money were at a higher rate than the bid price for one-year deposits," said another dealer.
The guilder was slightly stronger versus the German mark.
It was trading at 112.4825 per 100 marks against 112.49 on Tuesday.
